title: Scenario-Based Comprehensive Practice Exam (100 MCQs)
lessons: 4. How you'll work with Claude on your desktop
11. Claude in action: use-cases by role
12. Other ways to work with Claude
note: Independently authored practice questions with plausible distractors and scenario-based items. Not official exam questions or a guarantee of certification results. Verify changing product details with current official course guidance.

questions.prompt: A manager wants to use Claude's polished answer in a board pack without checking it. What should the manager do?
options: Treat it as correct because the board pack needs a decisive answer.
Verify material claims against authoritative sources and correct unsupported statements before sharing.
Ask a second chat to repeat the answer and trust it if both agree.
Keep it unless someone has already pointed out a contradiction.
questions.explanation: Verify material claims against authoritative sources and correct unsupported statements before sharing.

questions.prompt: A colleague cites a study that you cannot locate after Claude named it. What is the safest next step?
options: Assume the study exists because Claude supplied a plausible title.
Replace the citation with another paper without checking it.
Ask Claude to confirm the citation and accept that confirmation as proof.
Independently locate the study and verify it supports the claim; qualify or remove anything unverifiable.
questions.explanation: Independently locate the study and verify it supports the claim; qualify or remove anything unverifiable.

questions.prompt: Your team needs a policy that may have changed this week. How should you obtain the answer?
options: Check a current authoritative policy source and verify its date and scope.
Use Claude's stored knowledge because it can infer recent policy changes.
Compare several unsourced answers and choose the most common one.
Use last year's policy unless search snippets show a change.
questions.explanation: Check a current authoritative policy source and verify its date and scope.

questions.prompt: What is the safest assumption about a fluent answer from Claude?
options: Treat a confident tone as proof that a claim is true.
Ask another chat to repeat the claim and choose the majority answer.
It may still contain mistakes and needs verification when accuracy matters
Assume an answer is reliable if it contains specific details.
questions.explanation: A confident tone is not evidence that a claim is true.

questions.prompt: What is Constitutional AI intended to support?
options: Treat a confident tone as proof that a claim is true.
Guiding model behavior with principles intended to make it more helpful and safer
Ask another chat to repeat the claim and choose the majority answer.
Assume an answer is reliable if it contains specific details.
questions.explanation: Constitutional AI uses principles to guide behavior toward safer, more helpful responses.

questions.prompt: Why does Claude sometimes give an incorrect answer?
options: Treat a confident tone as proof that a claim is true.
Ask another chat to repeat the claim and choose the majority answer.
Assume an answer is reliable if it contains specific details.
Generative models can produce plausible text without guaranteeing factual correctness
questions.explanation: Generated text is not a guarantee of truth; verification is important.

questions.prompt: What does a model's context window refer to?
options: The amount of input and conversation content the model can consider in a request
Treat a confident tone as proof that a claim is true.
Ask another chat to repeat the claim and choose the majority answer.
Assume an answer is reliable if it contains specific details.
questions.explanation: Context windows are finite and model/feature-dependent.

questions.prompt: What does the course mean by selecting the right tool for a task?
options: Treat a confident tone as proof that a claim is true.
Ask another chat to repeat the claim and choose the majority answer.
Match the work pattern and available capability to the task
Assume an answer is reliable if it contains specific details.
questions.explanation: Tool choice should fit the task, workflow, and permissions.

questions.prompt: You ask for a launch plan but receive generic advice. Which prompt revision is most likely to improve it?
options: Ask for a longer plan without adding business context.
Add the audience, launch date, constraints, owners, risks, and specific deliverables to the prompt.
Tell Claude to act as an expert strategist but provide no project details.
Ask for three plans and choose the longest.
questions.explanation: Add the audience, launch date, constraints, owners, risks, and specific deliverables to the prompt.

questions.prompt: Claude keeps assuming the application runs on AWS, but your team uses Google Cloud. What should you change?
options: Keep the AWS assumption but request a more concise answer.
Remove cloud-specific details so the model can choose the common platform.
Ask for an AWS/Google Cloud comparison without saying which platform the team uses.
State Google Cloud and relevant architecture constraints explicitly, then verify the revised answer uses them.
questions.explanation: State Google Cloud and relevant architecture constraints explicitly, then verify the revised answer uses them.

questions.prompt: You need JSON consumed by a script. How should you specify and validate the output?
options: Specify the schema and allowed fields, require JSON only, then parse and validate it in code.
Ask for a formatted table because tables resemble structured data.
Request JSON and assume it will always parse correctly.
Allow commentary around the JSON so the script has context.
questions.explanation: Specify the schema and allowed fields, require JSON only, then parse and validate it in code.

questions.prompt: Your first response is too generic. What is the best next step?

Ask for more words without explaining what is missing.
Add the missing context, constraints, examples, or output criteria
Remove constraints so the model can choose the output format.
questions.explanation: Refine the prompt based on the mismatch rather than merely repeating it.

options: Add a role label but leave the task and constraints unspecified.
It helps make the response easier to use, compare, or process
Ask for more words without explaining what is missing.
Remove constraints so the model can choose the output format.

Ask for more words without explaining what is missing.

Add a role label but leave the task and constraints unspecified.

questions.prompt: A ticket classifier works on easy examples but fails on unusual cases. What should the team do before rollout?
options: Test only common examples and launch if those pass.

questions.explanation: Evaluate a representative labelled set, include edge cases, inspect errors, and define a human-review threshold.

questions.prompt: A spreadsheet formula generated by Claude looks plausible. How should you verify it?

Ask Claude to confirm the formula and treat that as independent verification.

questions.explanation: Test known cases, inspect references and edge cases, and reconcile results with source data.

questions.prompt: A team wants to compare two prompt versions fairly. Which test design is best?
options: Run both prompts on the same representative cases and compare using predefined criteria.
Use different requests for each prompt so each can show its strengths.
Choose the version that produces longer explanations.
Ask the model which prompt it prefers.
questions.explanation: Run both prompts on the same representative cases and compare using predefined criteria.

Ask the model to certify that its own output is correct.
Delegation

options: Test only easy examples and assume edge cases will behave similarly.
Discernment

Use writing quality as the main measure of analytical accuracy.

Ask the model to certify that its own output is correct.

questions.prompt: An AI workflow drafts an email with an unverified delivery date and can send it. What should happen next?
options: Send the email because most of the workflow is complete.
Pause sending, verify the date with an authoritative source, and review the final message before sending.

questions.prompt: A file-editing agent proposes changing files outside the agreed folder. What is the correct response?
options: Allow the change because the agent may need extra files.
Grant access to the whole repository to avoid interruptions.

questions.prompt: Which work pattern fits delegating a multi-step task over files and connected tools?
options: Grant broader permissions to avoid interruptions.
Let the workflow continue when a consequential detail is unverified.

Restart every step without checking what has already changed.
questions.explanation: Cowork is designed around multi-step task handoffs and working with files/tools.

questions.prompt: Why should you preview or inspect files Claude creates?
options: Grant broader permissions to avoid interruptions.
The file may not satisfy formatting, content, or business requirements until reviewed
Let the workflow continue when a consequential detail is unverified.
Restart every step without checking what has already changed.

Let the workflow continue when a consequential detail is unverified.

questions.prompt: What is important when using scheduled or automated task features?
options: Check availability, execution conditions, permissions, and output before relying on it
Grant broader permissions to avoid interruptions.
Let the workflow continue when a consequential detail is unverified.
Restart every step without checking what has already changed.

options: Grant broader permissions to avoid interruptions.

Restart every step without checking what has already changed.

questions.prompt: Two Project reference documents show different reimbursement limits. How should Claude's answer be grounded?
